scope.reference_only: Factory Asset V2 H01-025/H01-026 lifecycle semantics

objective: Replace always-on V1 browser ownership with job-scoped headful ownership while preserving persistent authenticated profiles, MUXIA/Hermes provider behavior, exactly-once dispatch and V1 product semantics.

hard_invariants.persistent_profile_identity: Profile/session state remains on disk across jobs; profile directories are never copied into per-job temporary identities.
hard_invariants.idle_zero_browser_owners: When no admitted job or Founder repair lease exists, V1 owns zero Chrome/Brave renderer roots for governed production profiles and exposes no browser CDP listener.
hard_invariants.one_spawn_per_job: Each admitted V1 job gets one bounded headful browser owner from its selected persistent profile; browser owners are not shared between concurrent jobs.
hard_invariants.exclusive_profile_owner: A governed persistent profile may have at most one browser owner or Founder repair owner at a time.
hard_invariants.loopback_cdp: Automated work may expose CDP only on 127.0.0.1 and only for the bounded automated phase.
hard_invariants.terminal_before_close: A durable terminal or committed-unresolved reconciliation receipt must exist before normal Browser.close.
hard_invariants.closure_proof: Completion requires browser root exit, CDP disappearance and release of profile/browser lease or mutex.
hard_invariants.profile_secret_boundary: No lifecycle component reads, exports or copies cookie/token/session credential bytes.
hard_invariants.provider_behavior_preserved: Existing V1 provider adapters/readiness classification/output acquisition/lineage remain semantically unchanged unless FA-338 explicitly migrates an ownership boundary.
hard_invariants.exactly_once_preserved: A committed provider dispatch may never be automatically repeated because a browser closed, crashed, timed out or entered protection challenge.
hard_invariants.lightweight_control_plane_allowed: Scheduler/broker/control processes may remain resident while idle if they own no browser process/context/CDP and do not hold a job lease.
hard_invariants.v2_identity_separation: FA-337 does not reuse h01-web-pNNN/h01-web-sNN identities and does not merge V1 with the V2 SVG engine.

protection_challenge_policy.pre_dispatch: Classify protection/auth challenge before provider commit, emit durable AUTH_REPAIR_REQUIRED disposition, close automated CDP browser, release job/profile browser ownership, and require Founder no-CDP repair on the same persistent profile before future automated admission.
protection_challenge_policy.post_dispatch: If dispatch may already be committed, emit COMMITTED_UNRESOLVED/reconciliation state and forbid automatic resubmission. Close the browser only after durable uncertainty/reconciliation evidence is written.
protection_challenge_policy.founder_repair: Founder repair uses the same persistent profile, headful browser and no CDP; automation is paused/excluded for that profile for the entire repair lease. CAPTCHA/protection is solved only by the Founder/platform flow, never automated bypass.
protection_challenge_policy.repair_release: Founder closes/releases the repair browser; only then may readiness be re-probed by a fresh automated job.

ownership_split.scheduler: Admit job, select eligible V1 profile/provider/route, own durable job/dispatch lease and exactly-once state; must not itself own browser profile bytes.
ownership_split.job_browser_runtime: Spawn one headful browser from selected persistent profile, expose loopback CDP during work, enforce job/profile exclusivity, wait for durable terminal/reconciliation, close and prove process/CDP/lease release.
ownership_split.provider_worker: Attach only to the admitted job browser, perform live readiness before dispatch, submit at most once after authority claim, acquire provider-original output, write durable result.
ownership_split.founder_repair_runtime: Own exclusive no-CDP repair lease and interactive browser for authentication/checkpoint repair only.
ownership_split.postproduction: Consumes durable provider result/artifact and remains independent of browser ownership.

required_evidence: durable terminal or reconciliation receipt hash

failure_semantics.pre_dispatch_failure: Safe to close and release; scheduler may choose another eligible route only under existing governed reroute rules.
failure_semantics.post_dispatch_failure: No automatic retry; durable reconciliation required.
failure_semantics.browser_crash: Write durable lifecycle failure; preserve dispatch-commit truth; release ownership only after process/CDP absence is proven.
failure_semantics.close_timeout: Escalate bounded SIGTERM/kill only after durable result/reconciliation exists; record forced closure in lifecycle receipt.
failure_semantics.profile_busy: Fail closed; never attach a second owner to same persistent profile.

migration_plan.action: Introduce V1 job-browser runtime and lifecycle receipt around existing persistent V1 profiles without changing provider prompt/output semantics.
Move broker/provider workers from externally persistent browser attachment to per-job browser attachment; keep scheduler/control API stable where practical.
Wire Hermes production scheduling so browser spawn occurs only after admission and browser closure occurs after durable terminal/reconciliation.
Migrate applicable Executive/Division01 cognition ownership to bounded demand-driven semantics while preserving no-CDP Founder protection repair.
Acceptance gate: queue empty proves zero governed V1 browser roots/CDP listeners; a fresh job respawns from same persistent profile and retains authenticated state without credential-byte access.
Move governed headful browser surfaces to Founder-visible DISPLAY :12 workspace mapping and exclusive Founder handoff.
Finalize Founder filesystem operability/permission normalization independently of browser lifecycle ownership.

rollback.during_FA_338: Retain current external persistent owner units/config as disabled rollback material until demand-driven canary acceptance passes; do not delete persistent profiles.
rollback.rollback_trigger: Lifecycle canary cannot prove durable-result-before-close, session persistence, exactly-once behavior, or clean process/CDP/lease release.
